curriculum: US/international high-school mathematics (Algebra 1 → Geometry → Algebra 2 → Precalculus → Calculus, with Statistics alongside)
note: The allow-list for question generation and the vocabulary used to tag gaps, for learners outside the Japanese curriculum. Course names follow the sequence most international high schools recognise (Algebra 1, Geometry, ...), not a translation of 数学I〜C.

goals: Expand products of polynomials using the distributive property and the special products
Factor by pulling out a common factor, by pattern, and by splitting the middle term
Explain why you picked that factoring method for this expression

topics.topic: Real numbers, radicals and absolute value
goals: Explain the difference between rational and irrational numbers
Simplify radical expressions and rationalize a denominator
Remove absolute value bars by splitting into cases
Solve a linear equation or inequality using the properties of equality
Explain why the inequality sign flips when you multiply by a negative number
Show the solution of a compound inequality on a number line
Move between slope-intercept, point-slope and standard form
Explain what the slope and the intercept mean for the situation being modelled
Decide whether two lines are parallel or perpendicular from their slopes
Solve a system by graphing, substitution and elimination
Explain how you chose between substitution and elimination
Say what no solution and infinitely many solutions look like on the graph
Complete the square to find the vertex and the axis of symmetry
Explain what completing the square is actually doing to the graph
Sketch a parabola from its vertex form

topics.topic: Maximum and minimum of a quadratic
goals: Find the maximum or minimum value of a quadratic on a restricted domain
Explain why the answer depends on where the vertex sits relative to the interval
Handle the case where the vertex falls outside the interval

topics.topic: The quadratic formula and the discriminant
goals: Solve a quadratic by factoring, by the quadratic formula and by completing the square
Explain what the discriminant tells you about the number of real roots
Decide which solving method fits the equation in front of you
Apply the product, quotient and power rules for exponents
Explain what a zero, negative or fractional exponent means
Tell an exponential model apart from a linear one and say why
Write a number as a product of primes and read GCF and LCM off it
Explain why the prime factorization tells you the number of divisors
Choose between GCF and LCM for a word problem and justify the choice
Convert between base ten and another base
Explain what each digit position is worth in base n
Use remainders to decide divisibility and justify the rule
Write the converse, inverse and contrapositive of a statement
Explain the difference between a necessary and a sufficient condition
Lay out a two-column or paragraph proof and justify each step
Pick the right congruence or similarity criterion (SSS, SAS, ASA, AA)
Explain why the criterion you chose is enough to conclude congruence
Set up a proportion from similar triangles and solve it

topics.topic: Special segments and points of concurrency
goals: Locate the centroid, circumcenter, incenter and orthocenter
Explain what makes each centre special and where it comes from
Use the 2:1 centroid ratio and the perpendicular bisector property

topics.topic: Pythagorean theorem and special right triangles
goals: Apply the Pythagorean theorem and its converse
Explain how the 30-60-90 and 45-45-90 ratios come about
Decide when a triangle is right from its side lengths
Set up sin, cos and tan from a right triangle (SOH-CAH-TOA)
Explain how the ratios extend past 90° on the unit circle
Choose the ratio that matches the sides you were given and say why

topics.topic: Law of sines and law of cosines
goals: Apply the law of sines and the law of cosines to non-right triangles
Explain how you decide which law the given information calls for
Recognise the ambiguous case and say what makes it ambiguous
Find a triangle's area with (1/2)ab·sin C and with Heron's formula
Explain which area formula the given information supports
Cut a solid along a plane and solve the triangle you get
Use the inscribed angle theorem and the tangent-chord angle
Explain why an angle inscribed in a semicircle is a right angle
Decide when four points lie on one circle and justify it

topics.topic: Power of a point and constructions
goals: Apply the intersecting chords, secant and tangent-secant relationships
Explain why the three cases are one theorem in disguise
Carry out a compass-and-straightedge construction and justify the steps
Compute surface area and volume for prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres
Explain why scaling a length by k scales area by k² and volume by k³
Decide which formula a composite solid needs and justify the split

topics.topic: Polynomial division and the factor theorem
goals: Divide polynomials by long division and synthetic division
Explain what the remainder theorem and the factor theorem are saying
Use a root you found to factor the polynomial further
Expand a binomial power and pick out a specific term
Explain where the binomial coefficients come from in terms of counting
Connect Pascal's triangle to nCr

topics.topic: Complex numbers and relationships between roots
goals: Do arithmetic with complex numbers and with conjugates
Explain why non-real roots of a real polynomial come in conjugate pairs
Use the sum and product of roots instead of solving when it is faster
Solve a quadratic inequality from the sign of the factored form or the graph
Explain how the graph tells you which interval to keep
Handle a rational inequality without multiplying away the sign
Prove an inequality by comparing the difference with zero or by completing the square
Explain when the AM-GM inequality applies and when equality holds
Choose a proof strategy and justify why it fits the statement

topics.topic: Distance from a point to a line
goals: Apply the point-to-line distance formula
Explain what the formula is measuring geometrically
Decide between the formula and a perpendicular foot construction
Decide how a line and a circle meet by comparing the centre-to-line distance with the radius
Get the same answer with the discriminant of the substituted equation
Explain why you would choose one of the two methods over the other
Turn a condition on a moving point into an equation
Shade the region a system of inequalities describes
Explain why the boundary is included or excluded
Move between exponential and logarithmic form
Explain what a logarithm is asking for
Apply the product, quotient, power and change-of-base rules
Solve exponential and logarithmic equations and inequalities
Explain why the domain restriction has to be checked at the end
Say what happens to the inequality when the base is between 0 and 1

topics.topic: Arithmetic and geometric sequences and series
goals: Write the nth term and the sum of an arithmetic or geometric sequence
Explain where the sum formulas come from
Decide which model a sequence follows and justify it
Read and manipulate sums written in sigma notation
Use the difference sequence to find a formula for the nth term
Explain why telescoping works
Turn a recursive definition into an explicit formula
Write a proof by mathematical induction
Explain why the base case and the inductive step are both needed
Apply the angle sum, double angle and half angle formulas
Rewrite a sin θ + b cos θ in the form R sin(θ + α)
Explain what the harmonic form makes easy to see
Solve trigonometric equations and inequalities on a given interval
Explain how the unit circle produces every solution in the range
Read period, amplitude and shift off a graph and justify each

topics.topic: Vector operations and the dot product
goals: Add, subtract and scale vectors in component form
Explain what the dot product measures and why perpendicular vectors give zero
Find the angle between two vectors
Write points that divide a segment using position vectors
Prove collinearity and concurrency with vectors
Explain why the vector proof is shorter than the coordinate one here
Work with components, magnitude and dot products in 3-D
Write the equation of a line or plane with vectors
Explain how a 3-D problem reduces to a 2-D one you already know

topics.topic: The complex plane and polar form
goals: Convert a complex number between rectangular and polar form
Explain what multiplying by a complex number does geometrically
Apply De Moivre's theorem to powers and roots
Identify a parabola, ellipse or hyperbola from its equation
Explain what the focus and directrix definition is saying
Move between parametric and Cartesian descriptions of a curve
Evaluate limits of sequences, series and functions, including one-sided limits
Explain what an indeterminate form means and why it needs more work
Decide whether an infinite geometric series converges and justify it
Compute a derivative from the limit definition and from the power rule
Explain the derivative as a slope and as a rate of change
Write the equation of a tangent line at a point
Differentiate products, quotients and compositions
Differentiate trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions
Explain how you decided which rule to apply first
Build a sign chart for f′ and read increasing and decreasing intervals off it
Explain why a sign change of f′ marks a maximum or a minimum
Use the second derivative for concavity and inflection points
Set up and solve an optimization problem
Solve a related-rates problem by differentiating a relationship in time
Explain how you chose the variable to optimize and the constraint
Find an antiderivative and evaluate a definite integral
Explain the fundamental theorem of calculus in your own words
Set up the integral for the area between two curves and justify the limits
Integrate by u-substitution and by parts
Explain how you pick u, and why that choice makes the integral simpler
Change the limits correctly when you substitute
Find a volume of revolution by discs, washers or shells
Explain how a Riemann sum turns into an integral
Choose between the disc and the shell method and justify the choice
Compute the mean, median, mode and quartiles of a data set
Read a box plot and a histogram
Explain when the median describes the data better than the mean
Compute variance, standard deviation and the correlation coefficient
Explain what the standard deviation tells you that the range does not
Say why correlation is not causation, using the data in front of you
Count arrangements and selections with permutations and combinations
Explain how you decided whether order matters
Apply the addition and multiplication principles to a multi-stage count
Compute probabilities with the addition rule and complements
Explain when events are mutually exclusive and when they are independent
Decide whether the complement is the easier thing to count and say why
Apply the multiplication rule and Bayes-style reverse reasoning
Explain what conditioning on an event does to the sample space
Compute an expected value and say what it means for a repeated game

topics.topic: Random variables and the binomial distribution
goals: Build the probability distribution of a discrete random variable
Use the binomial mean and variance
Explain which conditions make a situation binomial

topics.topic: The normal distribution and confidence intervals
goals: Standardize to z-scores and read normal probabilities
Build a confidence interval for a mean
Explain what the confidence level does and does not promise
State a null and an alternative hypothesis for a claim
Explain what a p-value is measuring and what rejecting means
Decide whether the evidence supports rejecting the null and justify it
